Subject: Procurement questionnaire & on-prem requirements

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — ACME HealthTech is excited about Redwood's latency profile and the model controls. Our procurement team attached the standard questionnaire and we have two follow-up asks before legal will sign:

1) We require on-prem / VPC deployment with data residency in our AWS account (us-west-2).
2) We need contractual audit rights that allow an annual on-site inspection of systems that process ACME data (limited to production inference hosts), and the ability to request a copy of relevant logs and evidence for up to 24 months.

Commercial ask: the customer is requesting a 40% discount on list pricing for a 12-month committed capacity agreement if we can agree to the above.

I've attached the procurement questionnaire for your legal team to review. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate the audit language and an on-prem option that places inference instances in our VPC?

Best,

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Procurement questionnaire & on-prem requirements — technical notes

Evelyn / team — technical perspective below. Short answer: we can support a VPC-hosted inference footprint and produce logs, but on-site access to Redwood-managed hosts is a no-go unless we put strict controls in place. Alternatives and constraints: 

- VPC deployment: We can provision inference workers into ACME's AWS account (Dedicated private placement) with a Redwood control plane reachable over a customer-approved egress. This preserves required telemetry while keeping compute in their account.
- Audit: For an annual audit, we recommend a timeboxed, scoped remote audit with Redwood staff present. On-site physical access raises IP exposure (kernel access, disk images). If ACME insists on on-site, we can negotiate a supervised site visit with a signed scope and explicit non-invasive checklist: no disk removal, no root-level access, no copy of binaries.
- Logs & evidence: We can export audit logs (access logs, runtime request traces, redacted payloads) for up to 24 months. We will require a data request template and an approved list of auditors.
- KMS / HSM: ACME wants customer-managed keys — we support BYOK for encryption at rest. HSM-level hosting (hardware modules in customer's datacenter) is more complex and will materially increase cost.

Estimated cost impact (high-level): providing a supervised on-site audit + BYOK + 12-month committed discount results in immediate incremental operational overhead roughly estimated at 18-28% of the base hosting cost (people + audit coordination). If we push to a 3-year committed term, the incremental is more manageable and we can larger discount.

I can draft a scoped audit checklist and a deployment runbook if Legal gives the go-ahead.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment referenced: deployment_diagram_acme.png

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Ruth Conway <ruth.conway@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Procurement questionnaire & on-prem requirements — legal redlines

Team — reviewed the questionnaire and drafted redlines. Summary of legal position and proposed compromise: 

1) Audit clause: Redwood cannot permit unrestricted physical on-site access to Redwood-managed production hosts. We will accept a limited, supervised audit that meets the following conditions:
   - Scope limited to systems that process ACME data (production inference nodes only).
   - Audits are annual, pre-scheduled with 30 days' notice.
   - Auditors must be pre-approved and sign Redwood's auditor NDA.
   - No removal of hardware or copying of Redwood binaries; copies of logs provided by Redwood upon request.

2) Logs & retention: We will produce access logs and redacted request/response traces for up to 24 months, subject to data minimization and redaction of other customers' data.

3) Commercial concession: Redwood policy caps standard discounts at 25% for one-year commitments; anything larger requires executive sign-off. Given the operational burden, Legal recommends approval of up to 25% discount if ACME signs a 24-month committed Dedicated placement and accepts the supervised audit language above. If ACME insists on unsupervised on-site access or HSM on customer premises, decline or route to executive committee for a separate risk assessment.

I've attached a redlined contract (Redline_ACME_20260522.pdf) with the above edits. We need executive sign-off to permit (a) the supervised on-site audit exception and (b) a discount >25%.

—Marcus Lin
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redline_ACME_20260522.pdf

1) Supervised on-site audit to inspect production inference hosts that process ACME data (annual, scoped, auditors pre-approved, no binary or disk removal). Legal will require Redwood staff to supervise and a signed auditor NDA.

2) Commercial: ACME requests a 40% discount on a 12-month commitment. Legal advises cap at 25% unless execs approve greater concession; Sales is concerned because operational overhead is significant. Proposed commercial compromise for your approval: 25% discount for a 24-month committed Dedicated placement + Redwood-managed supervised audit + BYOK key support.

If you approve both the supervised-audit exception and the proposed commercial compromise (25% / 24 months), we will present the redlined contract to ACME and aim to have signature and DocuSign completed by 2026-05-28. If you want a call, I can set one up immediately.

Please reply with APPROVE / DECLINE / CALL and any conditions.

Thanks,
